slides.title: Rules that predict
slides.text: A model is a rule that predicts what will happen, like: distance = 2 × height. A simulation runs the rule so you can check it.
slides.alt: The ramp model set to distance = 2 × height: the Model column predicts 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 before any trial runs.
slides.say: A model is a rule that predicts what will happen, like: distance is 2 times the height. A simulation runs the rule so you can check it.

slides.title: Predict, compare, refine
slides.text: Predict with the model. Run real trials. Compare. If they disagree, change the model, not the data, and test again.
slides.alt: Refined to distance = 2 × height and run again: the trials sit close to the model, and Dot says the model fits.

focus.cue: Compared with real trials: the model fits

slides.title: The ramp
slides.text: With distance = 1 × height, every trial went farther than predicted, so the rule is too low. Raise it, run again, and the error gets smaller.
slides.alt: With distance = 1 × height every real trial goes farther than the model: each row is off by a lot.

focus.cue: The real trials go much farther
Off by a lot on every row

slides.title: One trial is not proof
slides.text: One lucky trial proves nothing. Compare the model with many results. To balance a game, test 20 runs, not one.
slides.alt: Game balance: 20 test runs at one jump power, each a tick or a cross, counted as finished or fell.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Model Makers and solve all 5 cases. Watch the error number: your job is to make it smaller.
